quiz_map.support: "Unanswerable" is a real result: if prompt logging was off, question 2 may have no evidence at all, and the report has to say so.

Microsoft documents `AppAccessContext.ClientAppId` as the ID of the Entra app that performed the access on behalf of the user, and `AADSessionId` as the Entra session ID of the sign-in performed by the app on behalf of the user.
Larger messages are split into 32 KB chunks, and `SequenceNumber` gives the order for reassembly.
It therefore sits inside `RequestMessages` or `input.inputBodyJson` of the following call.
A call with no matching record did not take effect, or took effect somewhere you are not logging.
`TimeGenerated` in the gateway LLM log is the date and time when request processing started.
Microsoft's documentation is direct about the limit: a result of no document attack does not establish that the document is trustworthy.
Link 1 of the proof fails: no instruction was present in anything the model received, and the complete input is on record.

ApiManagementGatewayLlmLog holds the content: RequestMessages is what was sent to the model and answers questions 2 and 3, and ResponseMessages is what the model returned and answers questions 4 and 5.
A SharePoint FileAccessed record names the file in ObjectId.
A clean sign-in removes one explanation, account takeover.
Compare the sessionId on the sign-in with AppAccessContext.AADSessionId on the audit record: equal values mean the action belongs to that sign-in.

So the RequestMessages of the second call is the one place where you can read exactly what the model was shown.
